concept.name: Liquidity
concept.definition: The ability to buy or sell an asset promptly in meaningful size without causing a substantial adverse price change or incurring unusually high cost.
concept.intuition: It describes the immediately available terms and ease of trading in an order-driven market.
concept.mechanics: Assess spread, depth, turnover, resilience, venue access, and size-dependent impact rather than relying on one quote or volume statistic.
concept.failure_modes: Displayed quotes and depth can cancel, fragment across venues, or vanish under stress, so snapshots can overstate executable liquidity.
concept.misconceptions: A quote or narrow spread is not a guarantee that a large order can trade at that price without delay or impact.
concept.example: Selling 100 shares moves a liquid stock negligibly, while selling the same fraction of a thin issue consumes several price levels.
